correctness.rationale: An all-length proof uses the exact binary earth-mover prefix-imbalance identity. In a minimal <=4-swap collision, any zero boundary allows splitting, repeated nonzero boundary heights allow equal-weight segment deletion, and a height of magnitude >=2 would force five distinct nonzero unit contributions. Therefore at most two internal boundaries remain, with opposite heights; a two-block cross-splice preserves equal weight and distance <=4, contradicting P squared correction. The single-symbol block case and a sharp witness are handled separately. Independently, BFS on all 66,196 ordered equal-weight binary word pairs of lengths 1–9 verified the distance identity; exhaustive nonempty P through block length 4 tested powers 2–5, and sharpness was directly verified. Finite checks are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: It resolves a named open finite-test-horizon case in 2026 work, replacing a four-block upper threshold by an optimal two-block test for every binary block length and every block set. It reduces an infinite family of correction tests to exactly one fixed-length test, via a structural cancellation and cross-splicing lemma; sharpness follows from a one-symbol block witness. This is a natural exact invariant, not an arbitrary finite table or numerical increment.
